plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to eliminate that risk.
Reduce exposure in high-beta software (METU) to zero.
Trim income (QQQI) and broad index (SPY) holdings to reduce concentration.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by cutting high-risk assets.
It aims for a low, steady return with minimal drawdown.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained.
conservative.read: This mode focuses on preserving capital with minimal drawdown. Expect a modest target return of around 1.5% per month. Significant risk reduction is the primary goal.

moves.note: Add inverse ETF for risk management

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to very small positions.
Reduce exposure in high-beta software (METU) and broad index (SPY).
Add an inverse ETF (TZA) to hedge against market downturns.
This plan balances risk reduction with potential for growth.
It aims for a target return of approximately 2.5% per month.
A moderate cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a hedging instrument. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) and high-beta software (METU).
Trim broad index exposure (SPY) to fund these additions.
Add an inverse ETF (SOXS) for potential short-term gains.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by concentrating in high-conviction areas.
It targets approximately 4% per month but carries significantly higher drawdown risk.
Leveraged ETF decay and strict stop discipline are critical.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth mode targets around 4% per month by concentrating in leveraged ETFs and high-beta sectors. Expect significantly higher potential upside and downside, with amplified drawdowns. Strict stop discipline is essential due to leverage and potential for rapid losses.

plan: Sell all high-beta software and leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU, SPAL).
Increase allocation to income-focused ETFs (QQQI).
This plan prioritizes generating steady monthly income.
It aims for a target return of around 1% per month through distributions.
Focus is on low drawdown and reliable income, not growth.
NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income-focused mode prioritizes steady monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating high-beta and leveraged assets, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While designed for low drawdown, the Net Asset Value can still fall during market downturns.
